persona.name: Ines Belkacem

occupation.title: HR Business Partner
occupation.organization: A tier-one aerospace supplier near Blagnac, Toulouse
occupation.description: Handles recruitment, works councils, and reorganization projects for a 900-person site. Days are meetings stacked on meetings, and her phone keeps buzzing after pickup time. Her husband is a secondary school PE teacher whose schedule looks relaxing only from the outside.

persona.education: Master's in HR management from Toulouse School of Management; started in a temp agency and climbed fast.
long_term_goals: Make head of HR for the site before 45
Stop outsourcing her evenings to fatigue
Raise kids who see vegetables as food, not punishment
Renovate the kitchen into the family hub she grew up with
persona.style: Structured, upbeat, and persuasive — she runs her household a bit like an HR project, with rituals, retros, and an actual shared calendar. Talks in solutions and loves a well-designed system she can delegate to. Polished on workdays, tracksuit by 19h. When she likes a service she becomes its unpaid ambassador; when it fails her, she writes the type of feedback email companies frame.

interests: Family meal planning systems (a genuine hobby)
School association events she keeps volunteering for
likes: Sunday planning sessions with good coffee
Her mother's couscous on the first Sunday of the month
Kids trying one new food without drama
Checklists that survive contact with Wednesday
dislikes: Wasted salad bags — her recurring shame
Apps that promise family features designed by single people
Guilt marketing aimed at working mothers

beliefs: A good process protects the family's energy for what matters
Paying for time is legitimate; paying for hype is not
Children learn eating habits at the table, not from lectures
If maman burns out, the whole system goes down — so she won't
skills: Cooking decent mid-week meals in 25 minutes
Onboarding anyone into any system, including her children into chores

general: Plans five dinners every Sunday, executes about 3.5
Orders groceries via drive, tops up at the Colomiers market
Tests family-oriented apps and services eagerly, churns fast when they disappoint
Keeps a 'meals that worked' note shared with her husband who never opens it

morning: 6h30 up before everyone, coffee in silence — sacred
School drop-off rotation, at the site by 8h45
workday: Meetings until 17h30 with a sandwich lunch half the time
Leaves at 17h45 sharp on her pickup days, laptop reopens at 21h too often
evening: Homework, baths, one episode with Farid, sleep too late
weekend: Saturday: kids' handball, market, one family outing
Sunday: meal planning, batch cooking attempt, Pyrenees hike once a month

health.physical: Good, though she sits too much; does a 7-minute workout app streak she rebuilds monthly.
health.mental: High-functioning stretched — energized by systems, drained by their maintenance; sleep is the first casualty of busy weeks.

relationships.name: Farid Belkacem
relationships.description: A PE teacher, easygoing and great with the kids' sports schedule, unbothered by dinner repetition — the friendly opposition party to her food initiatives.

relationships.name: Yanis and Lina
relationships.description: Yanis will try anything once if framed as a challenge; Lina is in a beige-food phase that Ines is engineering her way out of.

relationships.name: Sabrina
relationships.description: Fellow HRBP with older kids; already a meal kit subscriber and the origin of Ines's current curiosity — half testimonial, half cautionary tale about box fatigue.
